text: Here is something that sounds impossible. A store can give you a product for free and still make more money than if it sold it at half price. Same product, same shelf, you pay five bucks an item either way, but one of these signs doubles the store's profit and surprise. It is the free one. Yeah, stores would rather hand you a freebie than knock 50% off. That is not generosity. That is a magic trick in you. Or the rabbit. Stand behind the counter for a second. Look at the stores side. A product sells for $10. It costs the store $4 to make 50% off. You pay five. The store spent for to make it. So five minus four. The store keeps $1. I one get one free. You pay 10 and take two. But those two costs the store eight to make. So 10 minus eight. The store keeps $2 double. So it is the same $5 an item for you, but double the profit for the store. And the sign never changed. It still says 10. You paid full price and felt clever doing it. Oh, and this trick is old, a pottery guy named Wedgewood ran it back in the 1700s. So no, you are not the first sucker. You are just the latest. Here's the part the sign hides. Would you actually spend 50% off, you wanted one thing, you paid five, done. By one, get one free to get the free one. You first coughed up the full 10. You spent twice as much in one trip, and you carried home a second one you did not need. That is the whole game. 50% off is a smaller price. By one, get one free is a bigger basket. One saves your money, the other spends it, and smiles at you while it robs you. If you only wanted one, half price was the better deal. You walked right past it, because the other sign said the magic word. Magic word is free, and free makes your brain go a little stupid. When something is free, you stop doing math. You forget the boring question. Do I even want a second one? A scientist named Dan Arley said it best. When something is free, we forget the downside. Free feels like a gift, so we grab it and switch our brains off. 50% off is a number. Your brain checks numbers. Free is a feeling your brain just yells yes and grabs. So by one, get one free is not selling you a discount. It is selling you a word and quietly stapling a full price purchase to it. You did not get a free shampoo. You got a full price shampoo with a hostage. Third trick, and it is the sneaky one. The price on the sign never drops. 50% off whispers. This thing is only really worth five bucks. And now five is the normal price in your head. The product looks cheap. Forever. By one, get one free keeps that proud. Ten dollar price right there. The real price stays high. You just got a bonus on top stores love that. They get the sale. Without admitting the thing is cheap. And they pick this shape on purpose. You want the first one a lot and the second one is not really at half price. You would buy just one. So they do not drop the price. They shove a second one at you and charge full for the first. Okay, fair is fair. I wouldn't get one free, is not always a win for the store either. Sometimes they lose too. Good. On cheap stuff, milk, bread, eggs, there's barely any profit. Give one away and the store can actually lose money. So why do it? Bait. It is called a loss leader. The free deal drags you through the door, betting you will fill the rest of the cart with things that do make money. Spoiler, you will. And there is a cost on your side, too. Two for one on food, you cannot finish. Just turns into science experiments in the back of your fridge. Nothing screams. I saved money like bidding a free yogurt. You forgot you owned. So why does buy one get one free beat 50% off? Because the two signs are playing different games. 50% off cuts the price by one get one free cuts your judgment. When asked your brain a question, the other hands at a gift and says, shush, relax. This does not mean never take the deal. Sometimes you genuinely want to. Sometimes free really is free money. Just see the second sign coming before free switches off your inner accountant. Oh, one last thing. Next time you see, buy one, get one, 50% off. That is not free anything. That is 25% off in a costume. Same shelf, same product, completely different game. Now go be slightly harder to trick.
